_comment: Emotion-tagged quote index. NOT retrieval content — loaded separately and used as an optional closing line after a technique, matched to the caller's emotional state. All quotes verbatim from the public-domain texts in data/classics/ (see each work's .md for translation and source URL). States must be from saathi.kb.emotion.STATES.

quotes.text: It is in thy power to retire into thyself, and to be at rest, and free from all businesses.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Let not things future trouble thee. For if necessity so require that they come to pass, thou shalt be provided for them with the same reason, by which whatsoever is now present, is made both tolerable and acceptable unto thee.
quotes.author: Marcus Aurelius

quotes.text: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: There are things which are within our power, and there are things which are beyond our power.
quotes.author: Epictetus

quotes.text: Calmness of mind is one of the beautiful jewels of wisdom. It is the result of long and patient effort in self-control.
quotes.author: James Allen

quotes.text: All that we are is the result of what we have thought: it is founded on our thoughts, it is made up of our thoughts.
quotes.author: The Dhammapada

quotes.text: The sovereign voluntary path to cheerfulness, if our spontaneous cheerfulness be lost, is to sit up cheerfully, to look round cheerfully, and to act and speak as if cheerfulness were already there.
quotes.author: William James

quotes.text: Unclamp, in a word, your intellectual and practical machinery, and let it run free; and the service it will do you will be twice as good.
quotes.author: William James

quotes.text: Keeping an equal heart, with equal mind bears shame and glory; with an equal peace takes heat and cold, pleasure and pain.
quotes.author: The Bhagavad-Gita
